correctness.rationale: Chebyshev conjugacy sends F_d^n to T_m with m=d^n and invariant arcsine angular measure. Orthogonality plus the product identity yields exactly the symmetric sparse C=I-2B matrix: for positive indices one half for |i-j|=m or i+j=m; the 0-to-m entry is 1/sqrt(2). Its nonzero graph decomposes into a degree-zero path, reflected residue-class paths, and possibly the even central self-loop path. Standard Chebyshev characteristic recurrences give all-K cosine root multisets and hence the complete B spectrum. For K<=m only two-vertex reflected pairs and possibly a 1/2 central self-loop survive; K<=ceil(m/2) is scalar, ceil(m/2)<K<=m has norm gap 1/4, and K=m+1 has gap 1/(2sqrt2). Each finite path angular-grid discrepancy <=1/L and there are <=floor(m/2)+1 paths, establishing the stated empirical arcsine bound and limit regimes. Independently constructed matrices for 450 (m,K) configurations agreed with all predicted eigenvalues within 1.8e-15. Finite checks confirm, not prove, unbounded n and K.
